intervals.quote: ARA comprises five independent autonomous stations, with an additional low threshold phased array merged with station 5, which were deployed at a depth of 100-200 m over the period 2012-2018

intervals.label: reduced-scale operation
intervals.note: Only 2 of 5 stations (A3 and A5+PA) are confirmed actively collecting data per the cited 2024 paper; the others await a planned upgrade. Status recorded as 'active' for the experiment overall to reflect that some stations are genuinely taking data now, per the brief's instruction to classify conservatively rather than default to 'active' -- this is a partial/degraded active state, documented in the note rather than overstated as full operation. Currency pass 2 (2026-10-25), no status change. The 2024 paper's 'planned upgrade' happened at least in part: arXiv:2509.18368 (September 2025) says "In 2024, two of the five ARA stations received DAQ upgrades" and describes the "2024-2025 season upgrades" of the ATRI-based DAQ, with RFSoC-based DAQ "foreseen in the coming years". Newer ARA abstracts treat the array as five stations 'taking data for over a decade' (ARENA, June 2026) with analyses of the 2013-2023 dataset and 'nearly 30 station-years of livetime' (arXiv:2603.00341, Lepton Photon symposium proceedings submitted 27 February 2026); none reports which stations are live in 2026 or the outcome of the 2025-26 and 2026-27 Antarctic seasons, so the 'reduced-scale operation' wording (2 of 5 live in the 2024 paper) is kept and may now be conservative.
intervals.quote: Currently A3 and A5+PA are currently collecting data; other stations are awaiting a planned instrument upgrade in the upcoming Antarctic summer season.

physics_goals.quote: an R&D device geared toward an IceCube-Gen2 radio detector
physics_goals.value: Search for the highest-energy astrophysical and cosmogenic neutrinos using in-ice radio (Askaryan-effect) detection, as an R&D pathfinder toward IceCube-Gen2's radio array

summary.plain: A handful of radio-antenna stations buried in the ice near the South Pole, testing technology for finding the highest-energy neutrinos from space and for a future upgrade to IceCube.
summary.technical: Askaryan Radio Array: five autonomous in-ice radio stations (100-200 m depth) deployed 2012-2018 near the South Pole, ~2 km from IceCube, as an R&D pathfinder for IceCube-Gen2's planned radio array. As of the collaboration's 2024 overview paper, only stations A3 and A5+PA (with its phased array) are actively collecting data; the others await a planned upgrade.
